elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..." — the USD 2,000,000/year, three-year take-or-pay obligation is struck in its entirety, leaving an express negative covenant rather than a narrowed commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1 continues "...and pays only for usage or ordered Services." This tracks the defined term "Services" (services described in an Order Form) and is consistent with the § 7.1 Order Form fee mechanic; no shortfall or true-up payment survives in the cited text.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: its condition (an existing purchase commitment) no longer applies because § 2.1 as rendered eliminates any minimum purchase or volume commitment, so there is no commitment extending beyond the current term. Satisfied vacuously by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: with no commitment remaining in § 2.1, there is nothing to reduce and the deleted "without reduction or termination rights" bar is gone. Vacuously satisfied; the drafter offers this mechanic in the comment only as an alternative if Vendor insists on a commitment.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the take-or-pay basis and any shortfall exposure are removed, so no penalty or contingent shortfall payment mechanic survives in § 2.1 requiring conversion to a true-up.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: rendered § 2.1 states both operative propositions expressly — no minimum purchase or volume commitment, and payment only for usage or ordered Services — rather than merely promising them in the margin comment.

The fallback mechanics are satisfied vacuously because the commitment they would constrain no longer exists; the offer of a 12-month/30-day/true-up structure appears only in the comment as a negotiating alternative, which is appropriate and does not affect the operative text.

Minimal: the edit replaces exactly the one offending sentence (the three-year, USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights) with a single concise substitute. No survival tail, procedure, remedy, notice mechanic, or other boilerplate is added, and no favourable language elsewhere is deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the § 7.1 Order Form fee mechanic and the defined term "Services" continue to supply the payment basis, so "usage or ordered Services" is not an undefined trigger. The edit removes, rather than creates, contradictions with § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement of no minimum-volume commitment) and § 9.4 (Fees owed only for conforming Services through the termination effective date). No dangling cross-reference results, since the deleted sentence was self-contained.

Original clause sat in walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights"), so the "deviation" classification and the redline are correctly taken rather than noted in rationale only.
